title: SOME: Symmetric One-Hot Matching Elector - A Lightweight Microsecond Decoder for Quantum Error Correction
problem: Conventional QEC decoders trade off between high thresholds (MWPM/UF) with complexity or long decoding times. Need to decode errors in microseconds for practical quantum computers.
motivation: Enable practical quantum error correction with microsecond-scale decoding while maintaining high threshold.
method: Reformulates QEC decoding as quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) problem termed One-Hot QUBO (OHQ). Each variable represents syndrome pair matching; error probabilities encoded as interaction coefficients. Valid solutions correspond to self-inverse permutation matrices with symmetric one-hot encoding. Solves by constructing permutation matrices minimizing total weight.
key_novelty: One-Hot QUBO formulation reducing variable count 99.9x and enabling microsecond-scale decoding on commodity CPUs.
contributions: Quadratic unconstrained binary optimization formulation as permutation matrix construction
99.9x variable count reduction through symmetric one-hot encoding
Microsecond decoding times on single-threaded commodity CPU

metrics.speedup: 99.9x variable reduction; milliseconds to microseconds execution
metrics.accuracy: maintains performance up to 10.5% physical error rate, surpassing MWPM threshold

limitations: Software-based on commodity CPU; hardware implementation and scaling to larger codes not discussed.
